title: Data Pad
textLines: You grab the data pad as the clanking grows louder, echoing down the corridor. Whatever's coming isn't trying to be stealthy.
You thumb through the cracked interface, eyes darting across half-dead menus until you spot a "Close Door" button—only it's grayed out,
an empty energy icon flashing beside it.
The doors need power.
Your gaze snaps to the laser pistol on the wall. It still has a single energy cell attached. The clanking is almost at the doorway now.
With no time to lose, you rip the cell from the weapon, the indicator light fading out as you sprint toward the far wall.
You scan frantically—then spot it: a narrow slot marked with a maintenance sigil. You jam the cell in.
The lights flicker. The floor hums beneath your boots. You slap the Close Door command on the pad.
With a metallic scream, the door slides shut just as a shadow rounds the corner. Its tall and human shaped
Bang. Bang. Bang.
The data pad chimes:
⚠ TEMPORARY POWER ESTABLISHED.
POWER CELL AT 9%.
ESTIMATED DURATION: 2 minutes.
You try to steady your breathing. The faint glow of the pad throws trembling reflections against the walls.
You swipe through its system files, searching for context—anything to tell you what's going on.
After a few tense moments, a schematic appears:
VESSEL: ARV Genesis Transit
CLASS: REDACTED Project Aequalis
The screen resolves into a wireframe map. Your current location flashes in yellow: Transport Bay - Project Aequalis
You blink. A transport chamber. That makes sense, that's probably how you ended up here.
If it brought you in… maybe it can get you out.
You open the transport console on the data pad and select Return to Point of Origin. The screen stutters, then flashes an error:
⚠ INSUFFICIENT ENERGY FOR LONG-DISTANCE TRANSPORT
So much for that idea.
You glance back at the schematic. The system lists other available destinations within the ship:
